packs.title: Square to Sea
packs.promise: Make three separate outings through squares, reading rooms and the sea fortress.

q.s: Turn two building details into a small fiction.
st: Enter the free museum through Aleksanterinkatu 16 during ordinary Monday to Friday 11:00–19:00 or weekend 11:00–17:00 hours. Use only a courtyard currently open to ordinary visitors; follow staff directions, use available first-floor storage as instructed, and keep the gateway clear. Pets are not admitted to the museum; service dogs may assist their owner.
Observe two architectural details in the open courtyard, such as the shape of an opening and a change of building material.
Write four original sentences about an imaginary object that could travel between those two details. Identify the object as fictional and connect both real observations to the story.
Keep private doorways, exhibits and other visitors out of the activity; no photograph, interview or purchase is needed.

Use ordinary public customer aisles in the Old Market Hall, Monday to Saturday 08:00–18:00; 31 October 2026 is 10:00–17:00. Individual vendors can keep different hours. No Sunday opening, purchase, stock item, seat or photography permission is assumed.
Find three currently visible display arrangements: a repeated shape, a colour contrast and a way objects are grouped. Observe without handling goods or blocking customers.
Write one short description for each arrangement and locate it by a nearby public aisle feature rather than a person’s name.
Compare which arrangement is easiest to recognise from a distance. No conversation, tasting or purchase is required.

q.s: Make room for a quiet interval.
st: Use an open ordinary central path in Esplanade Park. Stand clear of movement or use an available public seat; a seat, performance or particular planting is not guaranteed. No garden bed, restaurant or ticketed event is part of this pause.
Pause for five quiet minutes and notice three separate sounds or movements around the path.
Choose one detail that changes and one that stays nearly still.
Write two short notes about that contrast, without identifying or photographing strangers.

packs.title: Töölö in Detail
packs.promise: Explore connected Töölö streets and visitor spaces in two daytime afternoons.

q.s: Let the building prompt a composition of your own.
st: Use valid applicable Kunsthalle admission (€20 general, €12 for eligible reduced categories with proof, under 18 free or another documented entitlement). Ordinary Tuesday and Friday 11:00–18:00, Wednesday and Thursday 11:00–18:00, weekend 11:00–17:00; Monday closed. It is closed 2–20 November 2026, and 30 October opens only 11:00–14:00. The Nervanderinkatu 3 main entrance has 29 steps; the Ainonkatu 3 rear accessible entrance needs the bell and staff assistance, with a heavy door. Follow lobby storage and ice-cleat rules. Observe inside, then make the original response after exit.
In an open admitted visitor room, note two spatial forms in the architecture, avoiding a copied artwork or a claim about a particular current exhibition.
After exiting to safe ordinary public ground, turn those forms into an original composition of exactly three simple marks, or describe the three marks in words.
Explain which two observations prompted your response; do not draw on any surface or block the entrance.

q.s: Read the shore from dry public ground.
st: Approach by public streets and open dry landward paths, avoiding cemetery and temporary school grounds. Use the Arkadiankatu public pedestrian route and follow works signs. Seasonal lifeguards, toilets, cafés and bathing services are not promised outside their season. No swimming, water access, ice or natural-object collection is required.
From dry landward public ground, identify three different edges: between two surfaces, between an object and its background, and between a moving and a still feature.
Describe each in a short note and explain which one changes most as you shift your safe viewing position.
Leave every natural object and plant where it is; stay off piers, private structures and school grounds.

q.s: Compare the current vehicles and their labels.
st: The Tram Museum is free, ordinarily daily 11:00–17:00 at Töölönkatu 51 A. It closes 5 November 2026, 6 December, 24–25 December and 1 January, and closes at 16:00 on 20 and 27 November; private events can change access. Only guide and assistance dogs are admitted. Use the public museum entrance, not the working depot. Entry has a heavy door, thresholds and ramp limitations; do not assume the whole outing is step-free.
Choose two tram features currently available to ordinary visitors and record a related current label reference. No particular car or simulator is required.
Compare how the two features affect the passenger space or the way a vehicle is used.
Write one difference you could recognise again without copying a display panel or entering a staff-only vehicle.
